Figure 4.14: Compression and Liquefaction Layout 4.5.4 METERING ANALYZER PACKAGES Metering will be provided for the incoming CO pipeline, incoming rail and truck deliveries, export to ship, 2 and return vapor from the ship. The metering skids have been strategically placed near the CO supply 2 sources or outgoing CO products. The underground CO pipeline supply to the site will have a metering 2 2 package located near where the pipeline surfaces, just west of the CO storage tanks and east of the utility 2 area (see Section 4.5.8 Utilities). The CO supply from rail or truck will have their metering packages 2 situated just east of the loading arms area. The CO export and vapor return to and from the ship will have 2 Page68 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version metering packages positioned just west of liquefaction train 'A', near the north boundary area. Associated transfer pumps will also be located close to the metering skids. Fig. 4.15 provides a view of the metering packages and transfer pumps. Figure 4.15: Metering and Analyzer Package Locations 4.5.5 CO EXPORT SYSTEM 2 This facility features an export system consisting of 2x100% LCO Ship Loading Pumps, LCO metering 2 2 package, a CO gas return metering package, a vaporizer heater, and three loading arms on the ship berth 2 for the following services:  Offloading LCO 2 Page69 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version  CO vapor return 2  Spare arm capable of either service Based on similar projects, the loading arms will require platform access and room for maintenance access with the aid of mobile equipment (i.e. scissor lift, cranes, etc.) (see Fig. 4.17). The development and operational requirements of the area around the berth loading arms will be further refined during the FEED phase. There will be a pipe rack network traveling from the CO storage tanks to the Berth offloading arms. There 2 are areas of the pipe rack system which will have to be elevated to allow passage of roadways below. The pipe rack system will typically be 5 meters above any roadway or access point to provide ample clearance for larger vehicular traffic. Once the pipe rack reaches the northern boundary of the site it will travel due west towards the berth just south of and parallel to an existing LPG line.
